elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 3.2 retains automatic renewal ("will renew automatically for an additional term equal in duration to the previous term") and no mutual-written-agreement requirement was inserted, so the conditional automatic-renewal elements must all be satisfied — and they are not (see below).

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Renewal is "for an additional term equal in duration to the previous term of the applicable Service Option Attachment" — the renewal term is unbounded and mirrors an initial term that may exceed 12 months. To meet this element the operative text must state that each renewal term is twelve (12) months.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Rendered text requires written notice "at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term" — 60 days exceeds the 30-day preferred opt-out.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: No reminder obligation appears anywhere in the rendered language; the margin comment merely notes the preferred position includes a vendor reminder, which is not operative text.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the renewal provision permits only continuation "for an additional term equal in duration to the previous term" and contains no renewal uplift or repricing mechanic, so no cap is required within this clause.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 3.2 now reads "at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term", a 60-day window at the fallback ceiling. The deterministic check reporting "number not found" is a parsing artefact — the numeral is spelled and bracketed as "sixty (60)" — and the substantive window is 60 days.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the renewal clause grants no uplift right; renewal is on the same terms for a term equal to the previous term. The separate unilateral price-change mechanic elsewhere in the agreement is a change-of-terms right, not a renewal uplift, and is not part of this checklist.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the only operative change is "ninety (90)" → "sixty (60)", bringing the non-renewal notice window to the 60-day fallback ceiling, and the price-cap element is not engaged because the renewal clause carries no uplift right.

Minimality holds: a single numeral was changed. Mutuality of the notice right, the Service Option Attachment structure, the renewal mechanic and all surrounding words are retained verbatim; no survival tail, procedure or extra requirement was added.

Intent preserved: the clause remains an either-party non-renewal notice tied to the end of the then-current term; no defined term, cross-reference or commercial mechanic is left dangling or contradicted.

Preferred level is not reached and the drafter should note this if pressing further: to get there the clause would need (a) each renewal term fixed at twelve (12) months rather than "equal in duration to the previous term", (b) a 30-day Customer opt-out instead of 60 days, (c) an express Vendor obligation to remind Customer at least 60 days before each renewal, and (d) if any renewal uplift is later introduced, a cap at the lesser of CPI and 3%.

Watch-item outside the fallback checklist: because renewal duration mirrors the previous term, a multi-year initial term would produce automatic multi-year renewals, which the rule treats as walk-away territory. If any Service Option Attachment has a term longer than 12 months, escalate and add the 12-month renewal-term fix; on the current record the renewal-term length is a preferred-level point only, correctly noted rather than redlined.
Comment is accurate and proportionate: it states what changed, why (avoiding lock-in from an early deadline) and identifies 60 days as the fallback with 30 days plus a reminder as preferred.
